skills.name: Light sources
skills.description: Sort objects into things that make their own light (sun, lamp, candle) and things that only reflect light (moon, mirror, book).

skills.name: Shadows and blocking light
skills.description: Predict whether an object will make a shadow and which way the shadow falls, e.g. a toy with a lamp on its left casts a shadow to the right.

skills.name: Sound comes from vibration
skills.description: Pick which action makes a sound and what is vibrating, e.g. plucking a rubber band makes the band vibrate.

skills.name: Loud, soft, high, low
skills.description: Compare two sounds and say which is louder or higher, e.g. a whistle is higher than a drum.

skills.name: Living or non-living
skills.description: Sort pictures into living and non-living, e.g. a tree is living, a rock is not.

skills.name: Plant parts and jobs
skills.description: Match a plant part to its job, e.g. roots take in water, leaves catch sunlight.

skills.name: Animal body parts and uses
skills.description: Choose what an animal part is for, e.g. a duck's webbed feet help it swim.

skills.name: Senses and sense organs
skills.description: Match a sense to its organ and a situation where it is used, e.g. ears hear a bell.

skills.name: Match young to adult
skills.description: Match a baby animal to its parent, e.g. tadpole to frog, caterpillar to butterfly.

skills.name: Alike but not identical
skills.description: Decide which features a young animal shares with its parent and which may differ, e.g. a puppy has fur like its mother but may be a different colour.

skills.name: How parents help young survive
skills.description: Choose the behaviour that helps offspring survive, e.g. a bird brings food to chicks that chirp.

skills.name: Day and night
skills.description: Choose whether the sun, moon or stars can be seen at a given time, e.g. stars are seen at night.

skills.name: The sun's daily path
skills.description: Put pictures of the sun's position in order from sunrise to sunset, e.g. low east, high overhead, low west.

skills.name: Seasons and daylight
skills.description: Pick which season has the most daylight hours or match a season to a picture, e.g. summer has long days.

skills.name: Describe the weather
skills.description: Match a weather picture to its word, e.g. clouds and drops to rainy.

skills.name: Weather tools
skills.description: Choose the tool that measures a weather feature, e.g. a thermometer measures temperature.

skills.name: Prepare for the weather
skills.description: Pick the clothing or item that fits the weather, e.g. an umbrella for rain.

skills.name: Problem or solution
skills.description: Match a simple problem to a tool that solves it, e.g. a heavy box to a wagon.

skills.name: Pick the right material
skills.description: Choose a material for a purpose, e.g. a raincoat should be made of waterproof material.

skills.name: Try, test, improve
skills.description: Put the steps of making something better in order, e.g. build, test, notice problem, change.

skills.name: Solids, liquids and gases
skills.description: Sort everyday things into solid, liquid or gas, e.g. milk is a liquid, steam is a gas.

skills.name: Describe by properties
skills.description: Classify objects by colour, texture, hardness, flexibility or whether they float, e.g. a cork floats.

skills.name: Heating and cooling changes
skills.description: Predict what happens when something is heated or cooled and whether it can change back, e.g. melted ice can refreeze but a cooked egg cannot be uncooked.

skills.name: Take apart and rebuild
skills.description: Choose the set of small pieces that could be assembled into a given object, e.g. blocks into a tower.

skills.name: What plants need
skills.description: Pick which plant will grow best given sunlight and water, e.g. the one on a sunny windowsill that is watered.

skills.name: How seeds travel
skills.description: Match a seed to how it travels, e.g. a dandelion seed floats on wind, a burr sticks to fur.

skills.name: Pollinators
skills.description: Choose which animal carries pollen between flowers and why it visits, e.g. a bee visits for nectar.

skills.name: From seed to plant
skills.description: Put the growth of a bean plant in order: seed, sprout, seedling, flowering plant.

skills.name: Who lives where
skills.description: Match an animal or plant to the habitat it lives in, e.g. a camel to the desert.

skills.name: Compare habitats
skills.description: Choose how two habitats differ in water, temperature or plants, e.g. a rainforest is wetter than a desert.

skills.name: Many kinds of living things
skills.description: Decide which habitat picture shows more kinds of living things and group animals by body covering, e.g. fur, feathers, scales.

skills.name: Fast or slow change
skills.description: Sort Earth events into fast or slow, e.g. a volcano erupting is fast, a canyon forming is slow.

skills.name: Wind and water shape land
skills.description: Choose what wind or water did to a landform, e.g. a river carved a valley.

skills.name: Slowing erosion
skills.description: Pick the design that best stops soil or sand from washing or blowing away, e.g. planting grass on a slope.

skills.name: Name landforms
skills.description: Match a picture to its landform name, e.g. mountain, hill, valley, plain, island.

skills.name: Bodies of water
skills.description: Identify oceans, lakes, rivers and ponds and whether the water is salty or fresh, e.g. oceans are salty.

skills.name: Read a simple map
skills.description: Use a map key to locate land and water features, e.g. blue means water on the map.

skills.name: Ask, imagine, plan, create, improve
skills.description: Put the steps of the design process in order for a simple project, e.g. a bridge from paper.

skills.name: Compare two designs
skills.description: Given test results for two designs, choose which did better at the goal, e.g. the boat that held more coins.

skills.name: Sketches and models
skills.description: Choose which drawing or model shows how an object works and what a label points to, e.g. the wheel on a cart.

skills.name: Balanced and unbalanced forces
skills.description: Decide whether forces on an object are balanced and what happens, e.g. two equal pushes from opposite sides keep a box still.

skills.name: Predict motion from a pattern
skills.description: Predict where a moving object will be or go next from a repeating pattern, e.g. a swing returns to the same height.

skills.name: Magnets attract and repel
skills.description: Predict whether two magnet poles attract or repel and which objects a magnet picks up, e.g. N to S attracts, a paper clip is attracted.

skills.name: Static electricity
skills.description: Choose what happens when charged objects interact, e.g. a rubbed balloon sticks to a wall.

skills.name: Order life cycle stages
skills.description: Put the stages of a life cycle in order, e.g. egg, larva, pupa, adult butterfly.

skills.name: Compare life cycles
skills.description: Choose which organism has a given stage or how two life cycles differ, e.g. frogs have a tadpole stage, birds do not.

skills.name: Metamorphosis
skills.description: Classify animals by whether they go through metamorphosis, e.g. a beetle does, a dog does not.

skills.name: Build a food chain
skills.description: Order organisms so energy flows from producer to consumer, e.g. grass, grasshopper, frog, hawk.

skills.name: Producers, consumers and decomposers
skills.description: Sort organisms into producer, consumer or decomposer, e.g. oak tree is a producer, mushroom is a decomposer.

skills.name: Herbivore, carnivore, omnivore
skills.description: Classify an animal by what it eats, e.g. a rabbit is a herbivore, a bear is an omnivore.

skills.name: Who eats what
skills.description: Decide whether one organism eats another in a given biome, e.g. a grasshopper eats grass but not a frog.

skills.name: Habitats and who survives there
skills.description: Choose which organism can survive in a given habitat and why, e.g. a cactus survives in a desert because it stores water.

skills.name: Traits that help survival
skills.description: Match an adaptation to its benefit, e.g. thick fur keeps a polar bear warm.

skills.name: When environments change
skills.description: Predict what happens to organisms when a habitat changes, e.g. when a pond dries up frogs must move or die.

skills.name: Living in groups
skills.description: Choose how living in a group helps animals, e.g. a herd of zebras spots predators sooner.

skills.name: Inherited or learned
skills.description: Sort traits into inherited or learned, e.g. eye colour is inherited, riding a bike is learned.

skills.name: Variation in a group
skills.description: Choose a trait that varies among members of one species, e.g. dogs differ in fur colour.

skills.name: Environment affects traits
skills.description: Pick the environmental cause of a trait difference, e.g. a plant in shade grows shorter.

skills.name: Read weather data
skills.description: Read a bar graph or table of temperatures or rainfall and answer, e.g. which month was wettest.

skills.name: Climates of the world
skills.description: Match a region to its typical climate, e.g. polar regions are cold all year.

skills.name: Weather hazards and protection
skills.description: Choose the design that reduces damage from a weather hazard, e.g. a lightning rod protects a building.

skills.name: Fossils as clues
skills.description: Choose what a fossil tells about an organism, e.g. sharp teeth suggest a meat eater.

skills.name: Past environments
skills.description: Infer the past environment from fossils found, e.g. fish fossils on a mountain mean it was once underwater.

skills.name: Forms of energy
skills.description: Classify examples as light, sound, heat, motion or electrical energy, e.g. a ringing bell gives off sound energy.

skills.name: Energy transfer
skills.description: Trace how energy moves from one place to another, e.g. the sun warms a rock, the rock warms the air.

skills.name: Speed and energy
skills.description: Compare the energy of moving objects by speed, e.g. a faster ball has more energy and makes a bigger dent.

skills.name: Collisions
skills.description: Predict what happens to motion and energy when objects collide, e.g. a rolling marble hits a still one and the still one moves.

skills.name: Wavelength and amplitude
skills.description: Compare two drawn waves by wavelength and amplitude, e.g. taller wave has larger amplitude.

skills.name: Light, reflection and seeing
skills.description: Explain how we see an object by tracing light from source to object to eye, e.g. lamp to apple to eye.

skills.name: Sending information with patterns
skills.description: Decode or build a simple pattern code, e.g. dots and dashes spelling SOS.

skills.name: Energy flow in a food chain
skills.description: Trace energy from the sun through producers and consumers and tell where energy comes from at each step, e.g. a fox gets energy from the rabbit, which got it from plants.

skills.name: Plant structures and functions
skills.description: Match internal and external plant structures to functions, e.g. thorns protect, stem carries water.

skills.name: Animal structures and functions
skills.description: Match an animal structure to its function in survival, growth or reproduction, e.g. gills take oxygen from water.

skills.name: Senses send information to the brain
skills.description: Order how an animal responds to its surroundings: sense organ, signal to brain, brain decides, body responds.

skills.name: Rock layers tell time
skills.description: Order rock layers from oldest to youngest and infer past environments from fossils in them, e.g. bottom layer is oldest.

skills.name: Weathering, erosion, deposition
skills.description: Classify a described change as weathering, erosion or deposition, e.g. ice cracking rock is weathering.

skills.name: Patterns of Earth's features
skills.description: Use a map to find where volcanoes, earthquakes or mountains occur, e.g. volcanoes often sit near the edges of continents.

skills.name: Renewable or non-renewable
skills.description: Sort energy sources and resources into renewable and non-renewable, e.g. wind is renewable, coal is not.

skills.name: Where our energy comes from
skills.description: Match an energy source to how it makes electricity, e.g. dams use falling water.

skills.name: Impacts of using resources
skills.description: Choose an environmental effect of using a resource and a way to reduce it, e.g. burning coal pollutes air; using less electricity helps.

skills.name: Criteria and constraints
skills.description: Sort statements about a design problem into criteria (goals) and constraints (limits), e.g. must hold 1 kg is a criterion, only 10 straws is a constraint.

skills.name: Design a fair test
skills.description: Choose which test is fair because only one thing changes, e.g. same ramp height but different ball.

skills.name: Improve from results
skills.description: Given test data, pick the change most likely to improve the design, e.g. a wider base to stop tipping.

skills.name: Matter is made of particles
skills.description: Choose the particle picture that matches a state or event, e.g. gas particles spread far apart and fill a balloon.

skills.name: Mass is conserved
skills.description: Compute the total mass before and after a change, e.g. 50 g ice melts to 50 g water; 20 g salt plus 100 g water makes 120 g.

skills.name: Mixtures and separation
skills.description: Choose a way to separate a mixture, e.g. a magnet pulls iron filings from sand, evaporation recovers salt from water.

skills.name: Physical or chemical change
skills.description: Classify a change as physical or chemical using evidence, e.g. rusting is chemical, tearing paper is physical.

skills.name: Gravity pulls toward Earth's centre
skills.description: Predict the direction a dropped object moves anywhere on a globe, e.g. toward the centre of Earth, which looks 'down'.

skills.name: Brightness and distance
skills.description: Explain why the sun looks brighter than other stars by ranking stars by distance, e.g. the closest star looks brightest.

skills.name: Daily and seasonal shadow patterns
skills.description: Predict shadow length and direction from time of day or season, e.g. shortest shadow at noon.

skills.name: Stars change with the seasons
skills.description: Choose which constellations are visible in a given season and why, e.g. Orion appears in winter evenings in the north.

skills.name: Food webs
skills.description: Read a food web and identify what an organism eats, what eats it, and what happens when one population drops, e.g. fewer frogs means more insects.

skills.name: Decomposers recycle matter
skills.description: Order how matter moves from a dead leaf back to soil and new plants, e.g. leaf, fungi and bacteria, nutrients in soil, plant roots.

skills.name: Energy in food came from the sun
skills.description: Trace the energy in an animal's food back to sunlight, e.g. hamburger to cow to grass to sun.

skills.name: Keeping an ecosystem balanced
skills.description: Predict the effect of adding or removing a species from a web, e.g. removing wolves lets deer overgraze.

skills.name: Plants grow from air and water
skills.description: Choose where most of a plant's material comes from, e.g. carbon dioxide from air and water, not mainly soil.

skills.name: Photosynthesis inputs and outputs
skills.description: Sort sunlight, water, carbon dioxide, sugar and oxygen into inputs and outputs of photosynthesis.

skills.name: Plant experiments
skills.description: Choose the conclusion a plant-growth experiment supports, e.g. plants in dark grew pale so light is needed.

skills.name: Geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere
skills.description: Classify a feature by sphere and choose how two spheres interact, e.g. rain (hydrosphere) erodes rock (geosphere).

skills.name: Where Earth's water is
skills.description: Use percentages to compare water stores, e.g. about 97% of water is in oceans and most fresh water is ice.

skills.name: Protecting Earth's resources
skills.description: Match a human activity to its effect and a way to reduce the effect, e.g. fertiliser runoff harms rivers; buffer plants help.

skills.name: Identify variables
skills.description: Name the variable changed, measured and kept the same in an experiment, e.g. ramp height changed, distance measured.

skills.name: Read tables and graphs
skills.description: Pull a value or a difference from a data table or line graph, e.g. how many more cm the plant grew in week 3.

skills.name: Draw conclusions from evidence
skills.description: Choose the conclusion that the data support and reject claims that go beyond the data.

skills.name: Identify cell parts
skills.description: Name an organelle from a diagram or description, e.g. the nucleus holds the genetic material.

skills.name: Organelle functions
skills.description: Match an organelle to its job, e.g. mitochondria release energy, cell membrane controls what enters.

skills.name: Plant vs animal cells
skills.description: Sort structures by whether they appear in plant cells, animal cells or both, e.g. chloroplasts only in plant cells.

skills.name: Cell theory and microscopes
skills.description: Choose statements of cell theory and compute total magnification, e.g. 10x eyepiece with 40x objective is 400x.

skills.name: Organs and their systems
skills.description: Sort organs into body systems, e.g. lungs in respiratory, stomach in digestive.

skills.name: What each system does
skills.description: Match a system to its main function, e.g. circulatory transports oxygen and nutrients.

skills.name: Cells to organism
skills.description: Order the levels of organisation: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.

skills.name: Systems working together
skills.description: Choose which systems cooperate in a task, e.g. running uses muscular, skeletal, respiratory and circulatory.

skills.name: Kinetic and potential energy
skills.description: Compare kinetic or potential energy between situations, e.g. a ball at the top of a hill has more potential energy than halfway down.

skills.name: Conduction, convection, radiation
skills.description: Classify a heat-transfer example, e.g. a spoon warming in soup is conduction.

skills.name: Temperature, heat and particles
skills.description: Predict the direction heat flows and how particle motion changes, e.g. heat flows from the hot cup to the cold hand.

skills.name: Insulators and conductors
skills.description: Sort materials into good thermal conductors and insulators, e.g. copper conducts, wool insulates.

skills.name: Moon phases
skills.description: Order the moon phases or name the phase from a picture, e.g. new, waxing crescent, first quarter, full.

skills.name: Eclipses
skills.description: Choose the alignment that produces a solar or lunar eclipse, e.g. moon between sun and Earth gives a solar eclipse.

skills.name: Seasons and Earth's tilt
skills.description: Explain which hemisphere has summer from Earth's tilt position, e.g. northern tilted toward the sun means northern summer.

skills.name: The solar system
skills.description: Order the planets from the sun and classify them as rocky or gas giants, e.g. Jupiter is a gas giant.

skills.name: The water cycle
skills.description: Order or label water cycle processes, e.g. evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection.

skills.name: Air masses and fronts
skills.description: Predict the weather when a cold or warm front passes, e.g. a cold front brings storms then cooler clear air.

skills.name: Air pressure and wind
skills.description: Predict wind direction and weather from pressure, e.g. air moves from high to low pressure; low pressure brings clouds.

skills.name: Oceans and regional climate
skills.description: Choose how an ocean current or large body of water affects a coast's climate, e.g. warm currents give milder winters.

skills.name: Layers of Earth
skills.description: Order Earth's layers from surface to centre and match properties, e.g. crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.

skills.name: The rock cycle
skills.description: Choose which process turns one rock type into another, e.g. heat and pressure turn sedimentary into metamorphic.

skills.name: Igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic
skills.description: Classify a rock by how it formed, e.g. basalt from cooled lava is igneous.

skills.name: Write a testable hypothesis
skills.description: Choose the hypothesis that is testable and matches an if-then form, e.g. if salt is added then water boils at a higher temperature.

skills.name: Independent, dependent, controlled
skills.description: Label the variables and the control group in an experiment, e.g. fertiliser amount is independent, plant height is dependent.

skills.name: Interpret a graph
skills.description: Read values and trends from line and bar graphs, e.g. the temperature rose 4 degrees between 10:00 and 12:00.

skills.name: Element names and symbols
skills.description: Match element symbols to names and back for common elements, e.g. Na is sodium, O is oxygen.

skills.name: Atoms, molecules, compounds
skills.description: Classify a formula or model as element, molecule or compound and count atoms, e.g. CO2 has 3 atoms.

skills.name: States of matter and particle motion
skills.description: Predict how particle spacing and motion change during melting, boiling or cooling, e.g. boiling spreads particles far apart.

skills.name: Density
skills.description: Compute density from mass and volume and predict floating, e.g. 20 g in 10 mL is 2 g/mL so it sinks in water.

skills.name: DNA, genes and chromosomes
skills.description: Order from smallest to largest and define each, e.g. gene is a section of DNA, chromosome is coiled DNA.

skills.name: Dominant and recessive alleles
skills.description: Determine a phenotype from a genotype, e.g. Bb with B dominant for brown eyes shows brown.

skills.name: Punnett squares
skills.description: Complete a monohybrid cross and give the probability of an outcome, e.g. Bb x Bb gives 25% bb.

skills.name: Sexual and asexual reproduction
skills.description: Classify reproduction examples and compare offspring variation, e.g. budding in hydra is asexual with identical offspring.

skills.name: Limiting factors and carrying capacity
skills.description: Predict how a population changes when a resource changes, e.g. less water lowers the carrying capacity of deer.

skills.name: Competition and predation
skills.description: Read a predator-prey graph or classify an interaction, e.g. lynx numbers fall after hare numbers fall.

skills.name: Symbiosis
skills.description: Classify a relationship as mutualism, commensalism or parasitism, e.g. a tick on a dog is parasitism.

skills.name: Biodiversity and ecosystem health
skills.description: Compare biodiversity of two communities from species counts and predict resilience, e.g. the forest with 40 species recovers better.

skills.name: Types of plate boundaries
skills.description: Classify a boundary as convergent, divergent or transform from the motion or feature, e.g. a mid-ocean ridge is divergent.

skills.name: Earthquakes and volcanoes
skills.description: Predict where earthquakes and volcanoes occur from a plate map, e.g. along the Pacific Ring of Fire.

skills.name: Evidence for continental drift
skills.description: Choose which observations support moving continents, e.g. matching fossils on Africa and South America.

skills.name: Rates of plate motion
skills.description: Compute distance moved from rate and time, e.g. 5 cm per year for 1 million years is 50 km.

skills.name: Types and sources of pollution
skills.description: Match a pollutant to its source and the system it harms, e.g. fertiliser runoff to algae blooms in lakes.

skills.name: Greenhouse gases and climate
skills.description: Choose how greenhouse gases warm Earth and which activities emit them, e.g. burning fossil fuels releases CO2.

skills.name: Reducing our impact
skills.description: Match a problem to the most effective mitigation, e.g. overfishing to catch limits.

skills.name: Newton's three laws
skills.description: Match an everyday situation to the law it shows, e.g. a seatbelt holding you shows inertia (first law).

skills.name: Speed, distance and time
skills.description: Compute speed, distance or time, e.g. 120 km in 2 h is 60 km/h.

skills.name: Net force and acceleration
skills.description: Add forces along a line and use F = ma, e.g. 10 N right and 4 N left gives 6 N right; 6 N on 2 kg gives 3 m/s^2.

skills.name: Friction and gravity
skills.description: Predict how friction or gravity changes motion, e.g. a heavier object has more weight but the same free-fall acceleration.

skills.name: Define the problem precisely
skills.description: Choose the problem statement with clear criteria and constraints, e.g. a bridge that spans 30 cm and holds 500 g using 20 sticks.

skills.name: Prototype and test
skills.description: Order the steps of iterative testing and choose what to measure, e.g. build, load until failure, record mass.

skills.name: Evaluate trade-offs
skills.description: Use a decision matrix to pick the best design when criteria conflict, e.g. the cheapest design that still meets strength.

topics.name: Chemistry: formulas, bonding and the periodic table

skills.name: Read and build chemical formulas
skills.description: Count atoms of each element in a formula or assemble atoms into a named compound, e.g. H2O is 2 H and 1 O; build CO2 from one C and two O.

skills.name: Bonding and valence
skills.description: Use valence to decide how atoms combine and whether the bond is ionic or covalent, e.g. Na gives one electron to Cl to make NaCl (ionic).

skills.name: Periodic table groups and periods
skills.description: Place an element in its group or family and predict its properties, e.g. Cl is a halogen that is highly reactive.

skills.name: Signs of chemical reactions
skills.description: Identify evidence of a chemical reaction and label reactants and products, e.g. gas bubbles when vinegar meets baking soda.

skills.name: Wave speed, frequency, wavelength
skills.description: Compute one of speed, frequency or wavelength from the other two, e.g. 2 Hz and 3 m gives 6 m/s.

skills.name: The electromagnetic spectrum
skills.description: Order EM waves by wavelength or energy and match uses, e.g. radio, microwave, infrared, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma.

skills.name: Mechanical vs electromagnetic waves
skills.description: Classify waves and predict behaviour in a vacuum, e.g. sound needs a medium so it cannot travel in space.

skills.name: Reflection, refraction, absorption
skills.description: Predict what light does at a surface, e.g. light bends entering water (refraction).

skills.name: Series and parallel circuits
skills.description: Predict which bulbs light when a switch opens in a series or parallel circuit, e.g. in parallel the other bulb stays lit.

skills.name: Ohm's law
skills.description: Compute voltage, current or resistance, e.g. 12 V across 4 ohms gives 3 A.

skills.name: Electromagnets and motors
skills.description: Choose how to make an electromagnet stronger and what reversing current does, e.g. more coils gives a stronger field.

skills.name: Natural selection step by step
skills.description: Order the steps of natural selection for a scenario, e.g. variation, environmental pressure, differential survival, inherited change.

skills.name: The fossil record
skills.description: Infer relative age and change over time from fossil layers, e.g. simpler forms appear in older layers.

skills.name: Anatomical and embryo evidence
skills.description: Identify homologous structures and what they show about common ancestry, e.g. the bones in a bat wing and a human arm.

skills.name: Artificial selection
skills.description: Compare artificial and natural selection and predict breeding outcomes, e.g. choosing the biggest tomatoes each year.

skills.name: Relative dating
skills.description: Apply superposition and cross-cutting to order layers and intrusions, e.g. a fault is younger than the layers it cuts.

skills.name: Eras and major events
skills.description: Order major events in Earth's history, e.g. first life, first land plants, dinosaurs, mammals, humans.

skills.name: Half-life basics
skills.description: Compute how much of a sample remains after whole half-lives, e.g. after 2 half-lives 25% remains.

skills.name: Gravity depends on mass and distance
skills.description: Predict how gravitational force changes when mass or distance changes, e.g. doubling distance makes the force one quarter.

skills.name: Orbits
skills.description: Explain why planets and moons orbit and what happens if speed changes, e.g. gravity bends the straight-line path into an orbit.

skills.name: Scale of the universe
skills.description: Order objects by size and distance, e.g. moon, sun, solar system, Milky Way, universe.

skills.name: Choose the right graph
skills.description: Pick the best graph for data, e.g. a line graph for temperature over time, a bar graph for categories.

skills.name: Describe trends
skills.description: Describe the relationship in a scatter plot or table, e.g. as fertiliser increases height increases up to a point.

skills.name: Sources of error and repeat trials
skills.description: Choose why repeating trials helps and spot an outlier, e.g. the trial of 48 s among 20 to 22 s is an outlier.

skills.name: Balance chemical equations
skills.description: Balance simple equations, including those of photosynthesis and respiration, e.g. 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O.

skills.name: Biomolecules
skills.description: Classify molecules as carbohydrate, lipid, protein or nucleic acid and match monomers, e.g. amino acids build proteins.

skills.name: Properties of water
skills.description: Match a property of water to its biological importance, e.g. high heat capacity stabilises body temperature.

skills.name: pH and enzymes
skills.description: Classify solutions as acidic, basic or neutral and predict enzyme activity from pH or temperature, e.g. pH 2 is acidic; pepsin works best there.

skills.name: Organelle structure and function
skills.description: Match organelles to functions and classify cells as prokaryotic or eukaryotic, e.g. ribosomes make proteins; bacteria lack a nucleus.

skills.name: Membrane transport
skills.description: Predict the direction of diffusion or osmosis and classify transport as passive or active, e.g. water moves into a cell in a hypotonic solution.

skills.name: Cell cycle and mitosis
skills.description: Order the phases of mitosis and compute chromosome numbers, e.g. prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase; a 46-chromosome cell yields two 46-chromosome cells.

skills.name: Specialised cells
skills.description: Match a cell type to the structure that fits its job, e.g. a red blood cell has no nucleus to carry more oxygen.

skills.name: Photosynthesis
skills.description: Build the photosynthesis equation and locate stages, e.g. 6 CO2 + 6 H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6 O2 in the chloroplast.

skills.name: Cellular respiration
skills.description: Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration and order the stages, e.g. glycolysis, Krebs cycle, electron transport chain.

skills.name: ATP and energy transfer
skills.description: Choose how ATP stores and releases energy and estimate ATP yield, e.g. aerobic respiration yields about 30 to 32 ATP per glucose.

skills.name: Meiosis
skills.description: Compare meiosis with mitosis and compute chromosome numbers in gametes, e.g. human gametes have 23 chromosomes.

skills.name: Mendelian and non-Mendelian crosses
skills.description: Solve monohybrid, dihybrid, codominant and sex-linked problems, e.g. a 9:3:3:1 ratio from AaBb x AaBb.

skills.name: DNA structure and replication
skills.description: Write the complementary DNA strand and name parts of the double helix, e.g. ATGC pairs with TACG.

skills.name: Transcription and translation
skills.description: Transcribe DNA to mRNA and use a codon table to find amino acids, e.g. TAC becomes AUG which codes methionine.

skills.name: Lines of evidence
skills.description: Classify evidence as fossil, anatomical, molecular or biogeographical, e.g. similar DNA sequences in humans and chimpanzees is molecular.

skills.name: Mechanisms of evolution
skills.description: Identify natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow or mutation in a scenario, e.g. a storm randomly killing half a small population is drift.

skills.name: Speciation
skills.description: Order the steps that split one species into two, e.g. isolation, separate selection, reproductive incompatibility.

skills.name: Read phylogenetic trees
skills.description: Determine which organisms share the most recent common ancestor from a tree diagram.

skills.name: Energy pyramids and the 10% rule
skills.description: Compute energy available at each trophic level, e.g. 10,000 kJ in producers gives about 100 kJ at secondary consumers.

skills.name: Carbon, nitrogen and water cycles
skills.description: Place a process in its cycle and predict effects of changing it, e.g. deforestation lowers CO2 uptake.

skills.name: Population growth
skills.description: Classify growth as exponential or logistic and read carrying capacity from a graph, e.g. the curve levels off at 500 rabbits.

skills.name: Ecological succession
skills.description: Order the stages of primary or secondary succession, e.g. bare rock, lichens, grasses, shrubs, forest.

skills.name: Feedback loops
skills.description: Classify a response as negative or positive feedback and order its steps, e.g. sweating to cool the body is negative feedback.

skills.name: Immune response
skills.description: Order the steps of a specific immune response and classify immunity as innate or adaptive, e.g. antibodies after a vaccine are adaptive.

skills.name: Nervous and endocrine control
skills.description: Compare nerve and hormone signalling and match a hormone to its effect, e.g. insulin lowers blood glucose.

skills.name: Protons, neutrons, electrons
skills.description: Compute particle counts from atomic number and mass number, e.g. carbon-14 has 6 protons and 8 neutrons.

skills.name: Isotopes and ions
skills.description: Identify isotopes and compute charge or electron count, e.g. Mg2+ has 10 electrons.

skills.name: Electron configuration
skills.description: Write or pick the electron configuration and count valence electrons, e.g. oxygen is 1s2 2s2 2p4 with 6 valence electrons.

skills.name: Models of the atom
skills.description: Order historical atomic models and match each to its evidence, e.g. Rutherford's gold foil showed a dense nucleus.

skills.name: Periodic trends
skills.description: Compare atomic radius, ionisation energy or electronegativity between elements, e.g. F is more electronegative than Cl.

skills.name: Group properties and reactivity
skills.description: Predict reactivity and ion charge from the group, e.g. group 1 metals form +1 ions and react vigorously with water.

skills.name: Name and write ionic compounds
skills.description: Convert between names and formulas using charges, e.g. aluminium oxide is Al2O3.

skills.name: Name and write covalent compounds
skills.description: Use prefixes to name molecular compounds, e.g. N2O4 is dinitrogen tetroxide.

skills.name: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonds
skills.description: Classify a compound's bonding from its elements or properties, e.g. KBr is ionic, a conducting malleable solid is metallic.

skills.name: Lewis structures
skills.description: Count valence electrons and choose or build the correct Lewis structure, e.g. CO2 has two double bonds.

skills.name: Molecular shapes (VSEPR)
skills.description: Predict shape and bond angle from electron domains, e.g. NH3 is trigonal pyramidal at about 107 degrees.

skills.name: Polarity and intermolecular forces
skills.description: Decide if a molecule is polar and rank boiling points by intermolecular force, e.g. water has hydrogen bonding so it boils higher than methane.

skills.name: Classify reaction types
skills.description: Classify an equation as synthesis, decomposition, single or double replacement, or combustion, e.g. 2 H2O -> 2 H2 + O2 is decomposition.

skills.name: Balance complex equations
skills.description: Balance equations with polyatomic ions or combustion, e.g. C3H8 + 5 O2 -> 3 CO2 + 4 H2O.

skills.name: Predict products
skills.description: Predict products using the activity series or solubility rules, e.g. Zn + CuSO4 gives ZnSO4 + Cu.

skills.name: Oxidation and reduction
skills.description: Assign oxidation numbers and identify what is oxidised and reduced, e.g. in Zn + Cu2+ zinc is oxidised.

skills.name: Moles and molar mass
skills.description: Convert between grams, moles and particles, e.g. 36 g of water is 2 mol.

skills.name: Mole ratios
skills.description: Use coefficients to find moles or grams of product, e.g. 4 mol H2 with excess O2 gives 4 mol H2O.

skills.name: Limiting reactant
skills.description: Identify the limiting reactant and the amount of product it allows, e.g. 2 mol H2 and 2 mol O2: H2 limits, 2 mol H2O.

skills.name: Percent yield and composition
skills.description: Compute percent yield or percent composition, e.g. 8 g actual of 10 g theoretical is 80%.

skills.name: Molarity and dilution
skills.description: Compute concentration or dilution volumes, e.g. 0.5 mol in 2 L is 0.25 M; M1V1 = M2V2.

skills.name: Solubility and solubility curves
skills.description: Read a solubility curve and classify a solution as unsaturated, saturated or supersaturated.

skills.name: Gas laws
skills.description: Apply Boyle's, Charles's or the combined gas law, e.g. halving the volume at constant temperature doubles the pressure.

skills.name: Ideal gas law
skills.description: Solve PV = nRT for one variable, e.g. 1 mol at 273 K and 101.3 kPa occupies about 22.4 L.

skills.name: pH and concentration
skills.description: Convert between pH and hydrogen ion concentration, e.g. 0.001 M H+ is pH 3.

skills.name: Neutralisation and titration
skills.description: Write the salt formed and compute titration concentrations, e.g. HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O; 25 mL of 0.1 M NaOH neutralises 25 mL of 0.1 M HCl.

skills.name: Factors affecting rate
skills.description: Predict how temperature, concentration, surface area or a catalyst changes rate, e.g. powdered zinc reacts faster than a lump.

skills.name: Le Chatelier's principle
skills.description: Predict the shift when concentration, pressure or temperature changes, e.g. adding reactant shifts toward products.

skills.name: Motion graphs
skills.description: Read velocity from a position-time slope or displacement from a velocity-time area, e.g. a flat velocity-time line at 4 m/s for 3 s is 12 m.

skills.name: Kinematic equations
skills.description: Solve constant-acceleration problems, e.g. from rest at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s gives 25 m.

skills.name: Projectile motion
skills.description: Compute time of flight, range or height for a projectile, e.g. dropped from 20 m it falls for about 2 s.

skills.name: Vectors and components
skills.description: Add perpendicular vectors or resolve into components, e.g. 3 m east and 4 m north give 5 m.

skills.name: Newton's laws quantitatively
skills.description: Apply F = ma and action-reaction pairs, e.g. 20 N on 5 kg gives 4 m/s^2.

skills.name: Free-body diagrams
skills.description: Choose the correct free-body diagram or the net force for a scenario, e.g. a box on a table has weight down and normal force up.

skills.name: Friction and inclines
skills.description: Compute friction or acceleration on a slope, e.g. friction = 0.2 x 50 N = 10 N.

skills.name: Circular motion and gravitation
skills.description: Compute centripetal acceleration or gravitational force, e.g. v^2/r at 10 m/s and 5 m is 20 m/s^2.

skills.name: Work and kinetic energy
skills.description: Compute work and kinetic energy, e.g. 10 N over 3 m is 30 J; 2 kg at 3 m/s has 9 J.

skills.name: Conservation of energy
skills.description: Use energy conservation to find speed or height, e.g. dropped from 5 m it hits at about 10 m/s.

skills.name: Momentum and collisions
skills.description: Apply conservation of momentum to collisions, e.g. 2 kg at 3 m/s hits 1 kg at rest and they stick at 2 m/s.

skills.name: Power and efficiency
skills.description: Compute power and efficiency, e.g. 600 J in 10 s is 60 W; 40 J useful of 100 J in is 40%.

skills.name: Wave equation and periodic motion
skills.description: Relate period, frequency, wavelength and speed, e.g. period 0.5 s is 2 Hz.

skills.name: Interference and standing waves
skills.description: Classify constructive and destructive interference and compute harmonics, e.g. a 2 m string's fundamental has wavelength 4 m.

skills.name: Reflection, refraction and Snell's law
skills.description: Apply the law of reflection and Snell's law, e.g. n1 sin i = n2 sin r.

skills.name: Lenses, mirrors and Doppler effect
skills.description: Use the thin lens equation and predict pitch shifts, e.g. an approaching siren sounds higher.

skills.name: Coulomb's law and electric fields
skills.description: Compute the force between charges or the field direction, e.g. doubling one charge doubles the force.

skills.name: Series and parallel circuits
skills.description: Compute equivalent resistance, current and voltage drops, e.g. two 6 ohm resistors in parallel give 3 ohms.

skills.name: Electrical power and energy
skills.description: Compute power and energy cost, e.g. P = IV; a 100 W bulb for 10 h uses 1 kWh.

skills.name: Capacitors
skills.description: Compute charge, capacitance or stored energy, e.g. Q = CV; 2 F at 3 V stores 6 C.

skills.name: Magnetic fields and forces
skills.description: Use the right-hand rule to find the force on a moving charge or a current-carrying wire.

skills.name: Electromagnetic induction
skills.description: Predict induced current from changing flux and compute EMF, e.g. faster coil motion gives larger EMF.

skills.name: Transformers and generators
skills.description: Compute transformer voltages from turn ratios, e.g. 100:200 turns doubles the voltage.

skills.name: Photons and the photoelectric effect
skills.description: Compute photon energy and predict electron emission, e.g. E = hf; higher frequency light ejects electrons.

skills.name: Nuclear decay and half-life
skills.description: Balance alpha and beta decay equations and compute remaining amounts, e.g. U-238 alpha decays to Th-234.

skills.name: Fission, fusion and E = mc^2
skills.description: Compare fission and fusion and compute energy from a mass defect, e.g. 1 kg of mass is 9 x 10^16 J.

skills.name: Special relativity basics
skills.description: Predict time dilation and length contraction qualitatively, e.g. a fast-moving clock runs slow to a stationary observer.

skills.name: Life cycle of stars
skills.description: Order the stages of a star's life by mass, e.g. nebula, main sequence, red giant, white dwarf for a sun-like star.

skills.name: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
skills.description: Place a star by temperature and luminosity and classify it, e.g. hot and dim is a white dwarf.

skills.name: Evidence for the Big Bang
skills.description: Match evidence to what it shows, e.g. redshift of galaxies to expansion, cosmic microwave background to early heat.

skills.name: Kepler's laws
skills.description: Use Kepler's third law to compare periods and distances, e.g. a planet at 4 AU has a period of 8 years.

skills.name: Radiometric dating
skills.description: Compute an age from half-life and remaining fraction, e.g. 12.5% of C-14 left means about 17,190 years.

skills.name: Major events in Earth's history
skills.description: Order events such as formation of the oceans, oxygenation of the atmosphere and mass extinctions.

skills.name: Tectonics and surface processes
skills.description: Explain how plate motion, mountain building and erosion interact, e.g. uplift increases weathering which draws down CO2.

skills.name: Natural hazards and risk
skills.description: Compare hazard probability and consequence to rank risk, e.g. a 1-in-100-year flood zone with dense housing.

skills.name: Earth's energy budget
skills.description: Balance incoming and outgoing energy and compute albedo effects, e.g. 30% reflected leaves 70% absorbed.

skills.name: Greenhouse effect and feedbacks
skills.description: Classify a feedback as positive or negative, e.g. melting ice lowering albedo is a positive feedback.

skills.name: Interpret climate records
skills.description: Read ice-core, temperature or CO2 time series and compute a rate of change, e.g. 280 to 420 ppm since 1850.

skills.name: Ocean-atmosphere interactions
skills.description: Predict regional effects of El Nino, ocean acidification or circulation changes, e.g. El Nino brings rain to Peru.

skills.name: Ecological footprint and sustainability
skills.description: Compute and compare resource use per person and judge sustainability, e.g. 3 Earths needed if everyone lived like country X.

skills.name: Threats to biodiversity
skills.description: Classify a threat as habitat loss, invasive species, pollution, overharvesting or climate change, e.g. zebra mussels are invasive.

skills.name: Water and soil resources
skills.description: Evaluate water use and soil degradation data and choose a management practice, e.g. drip irrigation cuts water loss.

skills.name: Pollution and remediation
skills.description: Match a pollutant to its treatment and predict bioaccumulation, e.g. mercury concentrates in top predators.

skills.name: Compare energy sources
skills.description: Rank energy sources by carbon emissions, cost or reliability from a data table, e.g. solar has near-zero operating emissions.

skills.name: Energy efficiency calculations
skills.description: Compute efficiency and energy savings, e.g. a 35% efficient plant delivers 350 MJ from 1000 MJ of fuel.

skills.name: Carbon accounting
skills.description: Compute emissions from activity data and emission factors, e.g. 100 L of petrol is about 230 kg CO2.

skills.name: Experimental design
skills.description: Identify controls, randomisation, blinding and sample size issues in a study, e.g. a placebo group makes a drug trial controlled.

skills.name: Hypothesis testing
skills.description: Decide whether results support or refute a hypothesis and whether the claim is falsifiable, e.g. a p-value below 0.05 indicates a significant difference.

skills.name: Theories, laws and models
skills.description: Classify statements as observation, law, theory or model, e.g. plate tectonics is a theory, F = ma is a law.

skills.name: Peer review, bias and ethics
skills.description: Spot sources of bias and judge the reliability of a claim, e.g. a study funded by the product's maker needs independent replication.

skills.name: Mean, median, spread
skills.description: Compute mean, median, range or standard deviation from a small data set, e.g. mean of 4, 6, 8 is 6.

skills.name: Correlation vs causation
skills.description: Decide whether data show correlation, causation or a confounding variable, e.g. ice cream sales and drowning both rise in summer.

skills.name: Uncertainty and significant figures
skills.description: Report results with correct significant figures and percent error, e.g. measured 9.6 vs 9.8 m/s^2 is about 2% error.

skills.name: Evaluate models and predictions
skills.description: Compare a model's predictions with data and judge its fit or limits, e.g. the linear model under-predicts after year 5.
